_comment: Master spec part 6: communications, business, design and trades.

source.document: Published discipline learning outcomes and curriculum areas

communication-studies.note: Units follow the discipline's canonical areas — theory and rhetoric, interpersonal and organisational communication, media and culture, and research methods.

lesson.title: Communication Theory
lesson.summary: How communication has been modelled — from transmission to meaning-making, McLuhan's medium and all.

lesson.title: Rhetoric: the Art of Persuasion
lesson.summary: The oldest communication science — Aristotle's appeals and how arguments actually move people.

lesson.title: Interpersonal Communication
lesson.summary: Communication between people — nonverbal signals, self-disclosure and how conflicts escalate or resolve.

lesson.title: Organisational Communication
lesson.summary: Communication as the organisation — networks, culture and why corporate messages fail.

lesson.title: Media, Framing and Culture
lesson.summary: Mass communication's effects — framing, representation and what audiences actually do with media.

lesson.title: Communication Research Methods
lesson.summary: How the field knows what it knows — surveys, experiments, discourse analysis and research ethics.

source.qualification: Cambridge IGCSE Development Studies 0453 (final published syllabus)

development-studies.note: Units follow the syllabus's subject content — development concepts and measurement, then the economic, social and political dimensions of development.

units.title: What is development?
topics: Measuring development: GDP, HDI and beyond

lesson.title: What Is Development?
lesson.summary: Defining and measuring development — GDP's limits, the HDI and the many dimensions of poverty.

lesson.title: Why Inequality Between Nations Persists
lesson.summary: The development gap's causes — colonial history, geography, institutions, debt and trade rules.

lesson.title: Paths of Economic Development
lesson.summary: How economies develop — the role of agriculture, industrialisation, aid and investment.

lesson.title: The Social Dimensions of Development
lesson.summary: Development as people — schooling, health, gender equality and the urban transition.

lesson.title: Governance and Development
lesson.summary: Institutions as destiny — governance, conflict and who gets a voice in development decisions.

lesson.title: The SDGs and Development Practice
lesson.summary: The modern framework — what the SDGs are, what has worked, and how projects are judged.

source.qualification: Certificate in Principles of Public Relations examination content
source.document: Published examination content areas and PRSA Code of Ethics

public-relations.note: Units follow the certification content areas — the profession's foundations, research and planning, communication channels, and ethics and law.

lesson.title: What Public Relations Is
lesson.summary: Defining PR — relationships with publics, how it differs from advertising, and its longer history than you think.

lesson.title: PR Research, Planning and Measurement
lesson.summary: PR as a managed process — research first, objectives that can be measured, and the death of counting clips.

lesson.title: PR Writing and Channels
lesson.summary: The craft side — writing that journalists actually use, and choosing channels by audience.

units.title: Media relations
topics: Owned, earned, shared and paid media

lesson.title: Media Relations
lesson.summary: Working with news — what journalists need, how pitching works and the PESO model.

lesson.title: Crisis Communication
lesson.summary: When it goes wrong publicly — the crisis lifecycle, first-hour discipline and rebuilding trust.

lesson.title: PR Ethics and Law
lesson.summary: The lines PR cannot cross — ethics codes, disclosure duties and the legal edges of persuasion.

source.qualification: SHRM BASK — Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge
source.document: Official published certification body of knowledge

human-resources.note: Units follow the SHRM BASK's behavioural and HR-expertise domains — people, organisation, workplace, with the behavioural competencies running across.

units.title: HR's role and the employment relationship

lesson.title: HR's Role and Legal Foundations
lesson.summary: What HR is for — the employment relationship, the legal floor and the profession's ethical duties.

lesson.title: Talent Acquisition
lesson.summary: Hiring well and legally — planning, structured selection and why onboarding decides retention.

lesson.title: Learning, Development and Performance
lesson.summary: Growing people — training that transfers, careers and the modern (humane) performance review.

lesson.title: Compensation and Benefits
lesson.summary: The money architecture — pay structures, benefits strategy and the law and ethics of pay equity.

lesson.title: Employee Relations
lesson.summary: The day-to-day relationship — engagement evidence, fair process and working with unions.

lesson.title: HR Analytics and Strategy
lesson.summary: HR as a data discipline — measuring people outcomes and the changing nature of work itself.

source.board: Real Estate Business Institute / national licensing exam content
source.qualification: National real estate licensing examination content outline

real-estate.note: Units follow the national licensing exam's content areas — property and ownership, valuation, finance, contracts and agency law.

lesson.title: Property and Ownership
lesson.summary: What you actually buy — real versus personal property, estates in land and the rights that run with it.

lesson.title: Valuation and Appraisal
lesson.summary: What a property is worth — comparables, income capitalisation and replacement cost.

lesson.title: Real Estate Finance
lesson.summary: How property is paid for — loan mechanics, amortisation maths and what default actually triggers.

lesson.title: Contracts and Closings
lesson.summary: The paperwork of transfer — purchase contracts, escrow and the deed that finally moves title.

lesson.title: Agency, Disclosure and Fair Housing
lesson.summary: The licensee's legal spine — who represents whom, mandatory disclosures and fair housing duties.

source.qualification: AQA A-level Art and Design: Photography
source.document: Official specification (skills, knowledge and anthology requirements)

photography.note: Units follow the specification's requirements — technical foundations, the visual language of photography, genres and the personal investigation.

lesson.title: The Exposure Triangle
lesson.summary: The camera's three dials — aperture, shutter and ISO — and the creative trade-offs between them.

units.title: Composition and visual language
topics: Framing, rule of thirds and beyond

lesson.title: Composition and Light
lesson.summary: What makes a photograph read — framing, the quality of light and timing's role in meaning.

lesson.title: A Short History of Photography
lesson.summary: The canon — documentary truth, modernist form and the staged image's challenge to it.

lesson.title: Photography's Genres
lesson.summary: Three working genres and their traditions — the portrait's contract, the landscape's politics, the object's poetry.

lesson.title: Digital Workflow and the Print
lesson.summary: From sensor to paper — RAW processing, where editing becomes dishonest, and the print as the work.

lesson.title: The Personal Investigation
lesson.summary: Photography as authorship — building a body of work around an idea and writing about it critically.

source.board: University of the Arts London (UAL) — London College of Fashion
source.document: Published BA Fashion course structure and canon texts

fashion-design.note: Units follow the canonical fashion programme arc — design research and illustration, pattern cutting and construction, textiles, and the industry's system.

lesson.title: Fashion Design Research
lesson.summary: Where collections come from — research books, concept building and designing with references.

lesson.title: Fashion Illustration and Flats
lesson.summary: Communicating clothes on paper — croquis, technical flats and the portfolio that gets you hired.

lesson.title: Pattern Cutting and Construction
lesson.summary: From sketch to garment — blocks, darts, draping and the fittings where design meets the body.

lesson.title: Textiles: Fabric as Design Material
lesson.summary: Choosing and manipulating fabric — fibres, prints, drape behaviour and the sustainability imperative.

lesson.title: Collections and the Runway
lesson.summary: Design at collection scale — line-ups, styling and how the fashion calendar shapes creativity.

lesson.title: The Fashion System and Its Futures
lesson.summary: Fashion as industry — who makes decisions, the supply chain's human cost and the circular turn.

interior-design.note: Units follow CIDA's professional standards areas — design fundamentals, human-centred knowledge, interior materials and construction, and professional practice.

units.title: Design fundamentals and the design process

lesson.title: Interior Design Fundamentals
lesson.summary: The vocabulary of interiors — elements, principles and the process from brief to space plan.

lesson.title: Designing for People
lesson.summary: Interiors as behavioural technology — body measurements, accessibility law and how rooms shape behaviour.

lesson.title: Colour, Light and Sound Indoors
lesson.summary: The perceptual layer — colour in context, lighting layers and designing what a room sounds like.

lesson.title: Materials and Specification
lesson.summary: The material palette — specifying finishes and furniture, and what 'sustainable' actually certifies.

lesson.title: Interior Construction and Codes
lesson.summary: Interiors inside real buildings — systems, the code book and drawings a contractor can build from.

lesson.title: Interior Design Practice
lesson.summary: Running the practice — fees, liability, and designing from evidence rather than taste alone.

source.board: Society of Illustrators / university illustration curriculum model
source.document: Published programme structures and the field's professional canon

illustration.note: Units follow the BFA illustration arc — drawing and visual language, media and technique, the applied genres, and the business of illustration.

lesson.title: Drawing as Illustration's Root
lesson.summary: The trained hand — observation, composition and how illustrators find a voice without losing craft.

lesson.title: Illustration Media and Technique
lesson.summary: The material choices — pen and wash versus tablet workflows, and colour as narrative tool.

lesson.title: Editorial Illustration
lesson.summary: Pictures that argue — turning an article's idea into a single resonant image, on deadline.

lesson.title: Narrative Illustration
lesson.summary: Telling stories in images — picture-book sequences, characters that survive 32 pages, and covers.

lesson.title: Commercial Illustration
lesson.summary: Illustration as commerce — advertising, packaging, surface design and the motion crossover.

lesson.title: The Business of Illustration
lesson.summary: Surviving as an illustrator — contracts, usage rights, pricing and the ethics of the brief.

source.document: Official specification (recording, composition, listening and analysing)

music-technology.note: Units follow the specification's areas — recording practice, technology-based composition, listening and analysing production styles, and the history of the genre.

lesson.title: Recording Fundamentals
lesson.summary: Getting sound into the machine — mic types, placement logic and the discipline of gain staging.

lesson.title: Mixing and Production
lesson.summary: Making the record — the mixing toolkit and the listening skills that separate polish from noise.

lesson.title: Synthesis and Sound Design
lesson.summary: Making sounds from scratch — oscillators, filters, envelopes, sampling and MIDI's grammar.

lesson.title: The DAW as Instrument
lesson.summary: The modern studio in software — DAW architecture, editing grammar and automation as performance.

lesson.title: Production History and Styles
lesson.summary: How records came to sound — analogue craft, the digital turn and the producers who defined genres.

lesson.title: Mastering and Delivery
lesson.summary: The last mile — mastering decisions, the loudness wars' settlement and delivering to platforms.

source.board: ASE Education Foundation / National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence
source.qualification: ASE Education Foundation program standards and ASE certification test series (A1–A9)
source.document: Published program standards and certification test content

automotive-technology.note: Units follow the ASE A-series test areas — engine, drivetrain, electrical, brakes, suspension, steering, and the electronics that bind them.

lesson.title: Shop Safety and Service Basics
lesson.summary: The professional shop — safe lifting, tool discipline and reading factory service information.

lesson.title: Engine Repair
lesson.summary: Inside the four-stroke engine — diagnosing by compression and noise, and how repairs are scoped.

lesson.title: Automotive Electrical Systems
lesson.summary: The car as a network — batteries, circuits, sensor data and the ECU that decides everything.

lesson.title: Brakes, Steering and Suspension
lesson.summary: The safety systems — brake hydraulics, ABS logic and the geometry of alignment.

lesson.title: Drivetrain and Transmissions
lesson.summary: Getting power to the wheels — gearboxes, differentials and the hybrid systems now everywhere.

lesson.title: Emissions, ADAS and EV Safety
lesson.summary: The modern frontier — emissions testing, sensor calibration and the high-voltage discipline EVs demand.

source.qualification: AWS SENSE program and CW certification content
source.document: Published SENSE curriculum guidelines and certification requirements

welding.note: Units follow the AWS SENSE modules — safety, the major arc-welding processes, cutting, and inspection and codes.

lesson.title: Welding Safety First
lesson.summary: The non-negotiables — arc radiation, fumes and fire, and the protective systems around them.

lesson.title: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (Stick)
lesson.summary: The workhorse process — rods, polarities and running beads in every position.

lesson.title: MIG and Flux-cored Welding
lesson.summary: The wire-fed processes — spray and short-circuit transfer, flux-cored outdoors and aluminium quirks.

lesson.title: TIG Welding
lesson.summary: Precision arc welding — tungsten prep, filler control and the clean seams of stainless and aluminium.

lesson.title: Cutting and Joint Preparation
lesson.summary: Before the weld — oxy-fuel and plasma cutting, and why fit-up decides weld quality.

lesson.title: Metallurgy, Codes and Inspection
lesson.summary: The professional layer — what heat does to metal, weld symbols, and the codes that govern acceptance.

source.board: NCCER (National Center for Construction Education and Research)

construction-trades.note: Units follow the NCCER carpentry levels — site and safety, framing systems, exterior and interior finish.

lesson.title: Site Safety and Materials
lesson.summary: The job site's ground rules — fall protection, reading lumber grades and choosing fasteners.

lesson.title: Plans, Codes and Layout
lesson.summary: Building what was drawn — blueprint symbols, code minimums and the holy trinity of level, plumb, square.

lesson.title: Framing Systems
lesson.summary: The skeleton of a building — joists, studs, headers and the geometry of roofs.

lesson.title: The Exterior Envelope
lesson.summary: Keeping weather out — roofing layers, window flashing and the insulation strategy of the whole envelope.

lesson.title: Interior Finish Carpentry
lesson.summary: The visible craft — drywall, trim carpentry and the tolerances finish work demands.

lesson.title: Foundations, Concrete and Decks
lesson.summary: Where buildings start and end — footings, concrete craft and structural outdoor framing.

source.qualification: NFPA 1001 — Standard for Fire Fighter Professional Qualifications
source.document: Published standard's job performance requirements (Fire Fighter I and II)
source.track: professional qualification · Fire Fighter I & II JPRs

firefighting.note: Units follow NFPA 1001's job performance requirement areas — fire behaviour, equipment, response operations, and rescue and safety.

units.title: Fire behaviour and the fire triangle

lesson.title: Fire Behaviour
lesson.summary: Know the enemy — how fire grows, what flashover is, and the conditions that turn rooms into weapons.

lesson.title: PPE and Breathing Apparatus
lesson.summary: The suit that keeps you alive — turnout layers, SCBA discipline and managing your air.

lesson.title: Fire Attack and Water Supply
lesson.summary: Putting water on fire — hose lines, friction loss, hydrant supply and the modern interior attack.

lesson.title: Ladders, Ventilation and Entry
lesson.summary: Getting in, up and through — ladder work, cutting holes with purpose and defeating doors.

lesson.title: Rescue and Survival
lesson.summary: Saving others and yourself — search patterns, extrication basics and mayday procedures.

lesson.title: Hazmat, Prevention and the Service
lesson.summary: Beyond the fire — hazmat awareness, prevention work and how fire departments are organised.
